visualReview.notes: Actually inspected all 67 final images: 17 portable, 17 shared-material/geographic and 33 medium-fi. The oval enclosure, 38 bastions, mapped lake, two different temple groups, column stumps, cruciform rooms, open courts, western iwan spine, octagonal foundations and oblique red-stone hall remain identifiable. Removed the filled plateau slab and rebased local floors to Y0; only occupied masonry has buried feet. Added the documented modern protective canopy over the red-stone hall, with roof underside and four supports. Low gate views remain open; restoration arches do not become complete roofs. Four source turntables expose foundation feet because their stage has no ground; the lit scene places them below its relative plane. Small surface patches and regular shared masonry are stylized ruin detail. Current reference pixels inspected: Huff phase plans 1 and 4, the nomination’s lake/iwan photograph (PDF page74), Stefan Bschorer’s 2014 overview and Aryan Nasrollahi/Mehr’s 2017 iwan photo. None is copied into a model texture.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Five canonical reusable graphs supply limestone, travertine, brick, sandstone and painted metal. Carved stone and dark niches share tinted limestone; locally colored opaque PBR represents the mapped shallow water surface. Skyline uses each common graph’s linear mean in one draw. All six GLBs contain zero embedded images. Actual shared-material capture reads each graph once and unloading leaves zero live model geometries. The legacy review camera caused lake stripes in the overhead perspective; the existing --adaptive-clipping option removes that depth conflict without changing model height or engine code. Final shared lake views are clean. A flat review stage verifies relative contact and signed placement only, not measured Iranian terrain.

No synthetic neighborhood or flat stage is passed off as a surveyed site.

fidelityReview.notes: Accepted medium-fi exterior ruin reconstruction. The original817410-triangle,68898992-byte master remains exactly reproducible from the untouched original module. The reviewed version preserves the archaeological relationships visible in linked phase plans and photographs. Every surviving height, erosion profile, gate/tower station, fine wall position, canopy dimension and modern restoration detail is approximate. The22m iwan height is a proportional estimate. The20.5m red-stone hall side comes from the cited source; its modern26.4m canopy span and5.5m ridge are reconstructions. Temporary scaffolding, protective rails, finer ornament, surrounding village, Zendan/Belqeis and modern ticket buildings are omitted. Geological plateau, absolute elevation datum, real terrain slopes, lake bathymetry and channel continuity remain host-layer responsibilities; no numeric DTM or actual-terrain verification was obtained. The model includes a flat mapped lake color surface, so real water ownership/elevation must be coordinated with host terrain/water layers. Physical laptop/phone timings remain unmeasured.

legacyFidelityScope.notes: Maximum fidelity remains pending. Interior plans are visually registered approximations, not a photogrammetric survey. Individual wall positions, present erosion profiles and archaeological phase boundaries need measured refinement. Thirty-eight bastions are documented, but the tower stations and surviving heights are reconstructed. The north, old southeast and newer south entrances need local measured alignment. The west iwan is modeled as a broken northern wall with partial vault springing. Its 22 m remaining peak, broken edges, side niches and octagonal foundations are proportional estimates. No complete ancient roof is asserted. Fire-temple corner piers, restored arches, basins and column stumps are interpreted from plans and photographs. Exact restoration dates and current condition are unverified; temporary scaffolding is excluded. Shared stone, travertine, brick and sandstone are used without embedded images. The spring uses local PBR color, without bathymetry or a bespoke water shader. Small stones and weathering are procedural details. The plateau slab is provisional. Full geological mound, distant Zendan/Belqeis sites, surrounding village and modern visitor structures are outside this asset. Terrain fit and hydrology remain pending.
